criteria_notes.note: `test_make_conditional_deprecated` checks the warning. `test_etag_response`, `test_etag_response_412`, the `test_range_request_*` tests and `test_invalid_range_request` check it still works. `test_make_conditional_accept_ranges_string` and `test_make_conditional_request_object_and_post` cover the new branches (custom `Accept-Ranges` string, Request object input, non-GET/HEAD left untouched). Two behaviour differences: a failed precondition from `apply_conditions` (`PreconditionFailed`) is caught and turned into status 412, as before. An invalid Range header such as `bytes=-` is now ignored instead of raising 416, so I changed `test_invalid_range_request` to use the unsatisfiable range `bytes=20-30`.

`test_is_resource_modified_deprecated` and the parametrized `test_is_byte_range_valid_deprecated` in `tests/test_http.py` use `pytest.deprecated_call` and check the return values are unchanged. The old `is_resource_modified` tests are kept and assert the same results.

Old tests that call the deprecated functions are marked `filterwarnings` ignore so they pass under warnings-as-errors. No other source file calls the deprecated functions. The suite has not been run, so this is unverified.

summary: `make_conditional`, `http.is_resource_modified` and `http.is_byte_range_valid` now emit `DeprecationWarning`. I could not run the suite here, so none of these changes or tests have been run. `make_conditional` is reimplemented on `apply_conditions` and `apply_range`. I removed the private `_process_range_request` and `_is_range_request_processable`, since nothing else called them. The existing tests of the deprecated functions are kept, with the warning ignored via `filterwarnings`, rather than moved or removed.
